item.title: Site Fundementals
item.description:
Visit the Ownership Passover Steps to see how to transfer ownership of the site.
index.html is one HTML filethat contains everything for the websites frontend. This works in tandem with Supabase, which handles the back end data of the site. Vercel is used to actually host the website, providing the live link accessable to everyone. Please view Site Organization.canvas to see a visual on how all the platforms interact with each other.
External Libraries bring in external functionality for both Supabase functionality and excel tracking exporting functionality
Authentication is handled by Supabase - which includes sign in credential storage, invites, and module and lesson data. It also handles roles and permissions using Edge Functions
Vercel hosts the app itself, which is a single .html file running the full site.
When updating the site, the main aspect is adjusting the Github Repo. Click the link to the Github Repo page to learn more.
Use Supabases "SQL Editor" to update, add, or remove tables for the backend data (See Supabase for more info).
AI was heavily used in the creation of this project. Please review the AI Usage page for more details.

item.title: Features
item.description: Purpose: To standardize and expedite the training process as well as provide easily referenceable material and get new hires more confident in taking calls sooner.This will list all features included in the app, as well as how to get the most out of this training. It will be seperated into 2 parts, the admin features, and the user features. This will be 99% of what this site is used for. All users can access the training modules for their designated department to do the pre-written training. Each module can include lessons and quiz questions. These lessons and quizzes include some interacative material, which will be touched on later. These are seperated by department.These are quizzes OUTSIDE of the module "tests" once all lessons have been completed. These Quizzes can be created and sent individually to specific people. This was made as an alternative to the quizzes sent out to TS to "test your knowledge". These questions can include multiple choice, as well as long answer responses (that have to be graded manually by an admin/trainer).These guides are divided by department. The TS agents will not be able to access the CS reference guide, and vice verca. These reference guides are meant to be a simpler version of the OneNote. These pages include information such as modem types and pictures, quick access METS guide, and fiber gateway pictures and types. These can be quickly and easily edited by anyone with edit permissions (or can be given seperate permission to JUST edit reference guide).This section is also divided by department, however it is openly editable by each individual person. Each person will have their own notes section to use while going through the modules. Only the user can access these notes, and the formatting of the notes is similar to the reference guide. The search button at the top left is used to quickly find material within the modules and reference guide. The search starts broad and narrows down as you click through the options. For example, if you type "Modem", it will show you all modules that have that word, and you can choose to click into any one of them to find what you need. This button in the top left allows you to access your own settings. You can update your display name, your password, as well as your theme. Users can request admin access (which will be confirmed or denied by supervisors) here as well.You can seperate people in 2 ways. Teams are used to sort people into groups for filtering, such as people under a specific supervisor or people on a specific shift. This can also be used to seperate out new hires vs exisitng employees. Departments are indicitive of what modules the specific employees can access. Both of theses settings can be accessed in the "People" tab in the top right under your name. Under the "People" tab under your name in the top right, you can see everybody who is on the platform. You can search by name, as well as sort by team. From this area, you can create new users, edit existing user permissions, departments, passwords, and other user information. You can view each persons progress through all the modules for that specific department, by clicking on the person. You can see what lessons theyve viewed, as well as their quiz attempts and what they got wrong/right. All of this can be sorted through by alphabetical, most completed, least completed, team, and even by specific module. By default, supervisors are hidden from the progress screen, however they can be re-added with the checkbox at the top of the section. Here you can see the quizzes sent out to individuals and their answers. You can manually grade these (for long answer quizzes), and compare results between teams and people. In edit mode (accessed by hovering over your name in the top right and clicking "Enter Edit Mode"), you will be given the option to edit, create, and remove modules, lessons, quizzes, and the reference guide pages. This option will allow you to make announcements to specific people that will pop up in their inbox (or on their screen if they werent logged in at the time the announcement is sent). Usually I use this as an way to tell people about updates when they are made. The training app tracks most changes, including reference guide and module editing, account creation and deletion, and quiz creation. It also keeps track of the exact day and time these changes were made, as well as who made the changes and what was changed. Users can submit feedback in the bottom left hand corner. This feedback can be viewed by clicking the View Feedback button in the admin menu (under your name). You are not able to see WHO submitted the feedback, but it tracks what page they were on when it was submitted, so you can more easily track the problem.

item.title: Ownership Passover Steps
item.description: These are the following steps and information required to properly pass over site ownership.There are 3 main platforms that keep the site running, and all 3 need seperate transfering processes to pass ownership properly. GitHub transfers onloy work between two GitHub.com accounts. Make sure you have a GitHub account BEFORE starting the process. Open the repo → Settings Scroll to Danger Zone → click Transfer Type the new owner's username or organization name, confirm If transferring to an organization, you need permission to create repos in that org (or an org admin has to approve it) Check email for a transfer confirmation (personal-account transfers require this; org transfers may not send one) Accept the transfer Once accepted, you immediately have full admin rights — code, issues, PRs, settings Vercel transfers happen between teams, not people. Create a Vercel account Create a Vercel Team Add both the giving party to the team, and add the receiving party to the old team In the project, go to Settings → General, scroll to Transfer Project Click Transfer, select the destination team (or create one) Confirm the site is still up and running Accept team membership Verify everything is up and running This is the most important and high-staked transfer. This is the platform that houses all trainee data, progress, and module data is stored. Kind of like Vercel, project transfers happen between Organizations, not between Users. Create a new organization Add the receiving party to that organization (must be ATLEAST a member) Go to the projects *Settings -> General Initiate the transfer, select the target organization Confirm the transfer Verify everything is set up properly Verify the new owner has admin/supervisor access to make required changes and testing.

item.title: AI Usage
item.description: This training platform heavily relied on AI for its creation. AI allowed for very quick and efficient code edits and adjustment. All of the code, once the edits were made, was reviewed to verify integrity and accuracy. AI Used: Claude Model: Sonnet 5 Effort: Medium Other Details: I paid for the pro version of Claude for the credit boost. When using Claude, there is a usage limit based on the messages being sent, the size of the files involved, and the overall difficulty of the tasks at hand. Due to the sheer scale of the project file, and the code being edited, a higher usage limited was needed. I used the project feature of Claude to organize the files and conversations. Under a project, you can add files, and store all conversations about the project within that project. That kept all context of what youre working on in one place. It also allowed Claude to access the file youre working with to provide new code/edits. I had Claude provide the full code file everytime a change was made, then added it within Github. Once you edit the index.html file, you can "Preview" the changes, allowing you to see what was removed and added. This is where I reviewed the changes, as well as made adjustments if necessary. The preview section of Github allows you to see what lines were changed allowing for easy updates and changes.

item.title: Usage Information
item.description: Each platform used has specific rules needing to be followed for continued hosting and implementation. The project hosted on Vercel is currently considered a "Hobby team". Commercial Use for Hobby accounts is striclty prohitbited, and the Vercel website explicitly states what is considered Commercial Use. Commercial usage is defined as any Deployment that is used for the purpose of financial gain of anyone involved in any part of the production of the project, including a paid employee or consultant writing the code. Examples of this include, but are not limited to, the following: -Any method of requesting or processing payment from visitors of the site -Advertising the sale of a product or service -Receiving payment to create, update, or host the site -Affiliate linking is the primary purpose of the site -The inclusion of advertisements, including but not limited to online advertising platforms like Google AdSense Source: https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelinesDue to the nature of the site, it MAY be required to switch to either a pro account ($20/month), or switch to a different platform. I currently have tested with Cloudflare, which has less strict Use policies. This may require a domain to be bought, however it is significantly cheaper (around $10 a year). Switching hosting platforms KEEPS all the data intact I don't believe it will be a problem now, especially since Vercel doesn't do any sort of random auditing. Their "Fair Use" rules are governed by usage limits and traffic. We should never be near any of those limits based on the amount of people who will use the site at a time.

item.title: Supabase
item.description:
Supabase is the platform that handles the backend data for the website. This includes everything from the modules and lessons themsevles, to the indivudal user profiles and permission data. Edge Functions handles server side permissions like creating accounts, or generating the Tracker file. These functions can be found on the left side of the sidebar.
SQL is the langauge used by Supabase (as well as most websites) to store, edit, and retreive data. This data is stored as "tables", which make up rows and columns based on what data is being stored. Below is an example table for data storage. (It is a made up example, not pulled from the actual database)This data then gets pulled by the website itself to use. If Jane Doe, for example, completed more modules, the website would basically tell supabase: update Jane Doe's progress to 90%.The table editor in Supabase shows existing tables and data. These tables can be accessed, seen, and edited in the table editor, however a lot of the sensitive data is encrypted (such as passwords).

item.title: Edge Functions
Vercel
item.description: Serves the index file over a CDNWatches the Github Repo for changes, and auto deploys when changes are detectedCan preview deployments before changes go live to test out features on a live urlHTTPS + domain handling: automatically provisions SSL certificates and handles routing for the domain you point at the project. vercel.app is the default subdomain. All updates and versions are recorded through Vercel, which keeps a copy of the "Deployment" (or version) each update. If something breaks, or you need to go back a version, you can do one of 2 things. You can Instant Rollback to the latest version, or you can "Promote" as previous version.Under the "Deployments" tab on the left sidebar, you can see all previous and current versions. The one that says "Production" is the current version that is considered "Live". Clicking the 3 dots on the right of any Deployment will allow you to Promote it, which turns it into the Production Deployment.When you update the code in Github, and commit the changes, it will allow you to type a summary of the changes. This summary will auto pull to vercel so you can more easily choose the version you need to go live.

item.title: Github Repo
item.description: This platform holds the .html file itself. It gets monitored by Vercel for changes, allowing for auto deployment once changes are made to the Github page. When an update is needed to be made, go into the "index.html" file, click the "pencil" button in the top right, and adjust the code. Once the changes are made, "Commit changes" (save the changes), and wait about 10 seconds. The site should update, needing a refresh.
